script.title: Labour Variances: rate, efficiency, idle time
script.caption_hook: Labour cost went up. Who paid more, who took longer?

lines.say: Labour cost went up this month. Who paid more, who took longer?
A labour variance compares what labour should have cost with what it cost, then finds why.
Standard hours for actual output: 200 hours at ₹50 per hour. Paid: 220 hours at ₹52 per hour, ten idle.
Standard cost is ₹10,000. Actual is 220 times ₹52, ₹11,440. Standard minus actual: minus ₹1,440, adverse.
Adverse. But is it the rate or the hours?
Rate: standard rate minus actual rate, times hours paid. Minus ₹2 times 220 is minus ₹440.

board.title: Rate Variance
board.sub: AH paid = hours paid, including idle hours

lines.say: Wait, why hours paid? Ten hours were idle, no?
Idle hours are paid too, so rate uses them. Idle time variance: ten hours times ₹50, ₹500 adverse.
Hmm, so efficiency must use hours actually worked?
Yes! Worked hours: 220 minus 10, so 210. Standard 200 minus 210, times ₹50, is minus ₹500.

board.title: Labour Efficiency
board.sub: SH std hours; AH worked = paid − idle hours

lines.say: Oh! Minus 440, minus 500, minus 500. That's minus 1,440!
Perfect. Rate uses hours paid. Efficiency uses hours worked. Standard minus actual, always.
